ORDER Dated this the 27th day of October, 2020 This criminal revision petition is directed against the judgment dated 31.3.2005 in Crl.A.No.276/2001 on the file of the Additional Sessions Court (Ad M.I.Sunny vs State Of Kerala on 27 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105498302/
1 hoc)-I, Kottayam.
The revision petitioner was the 1st accused in S.T.No.14/1995 on the file of the Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Kottayam and the appellant in Crl.A.No.276/2001.

The original complaint was filed by the Food Inspector, Kottayam Municipality against the accused alleging commission of offences punishable under Sections 2(ia)
(a) (h) (j) (1) 7(i) 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,1954 (hereinafter referred to as 'the PFA Act') and Rules 24 and 28 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules.
2.
The prosecution case in brief is that on 19.12.1994 at about 2.30 pm. the Food Inspector, ..3..
Kottayam Municipality purchased three icing cakes of 500 gms each from the shop room of the petitioner in accordance with rules.

One of the samples was sent for analysis and the public analyst,
on analysis, reported that the sample contained non-permitted coal tar dye, Rhodamine B and therefore adulterated.
Hence, the complaint was filed.
3. The learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offence and issued summons to the accused.
On the appearance of the accused, particulars of the offence were read over to him to which he pleaded not guilty.
4. During the trial, the accused filed an application to implead the 2nd accused, the manufacturer of the icing cakes.
Accordingly, the 2nd accused was impleaded.
His presence could not be procured despite various coercive steps against him.
Hence, he was declared as an absconder during trial.
When the case came up for evidence PWs.1 and 2 were examined and marked Exts.P1 to P16 on prosecution side.
DWs.1 and 2 were examined and marked Ext.D1 on the side of the accused.

After having heard both sides, the learned Magistrate convicted and sentenced the accused to undergo simple imprisonment for six months and also to pay a fine of Rs.2,000/- and in default of payment of fine to undergo simple imprisonment for three months more under Section 16(1)
(a)(i) of the PFA Act.
The accused challenged the judgment in appeal.
The appeal was dismissed confirming the judgment of the trial court.
Hence, the revision petitioner has preferred this revision before this Court.
6. Heard both sides.
7. The prosecution was initiated based on Ext.P12 Form-III report received from the Public Analyst.
Ext.P14 Form-II report confirmed the finding in Ext.P12.

In ..5..
Pepsico India Holdings Pvt.Ltd. v. Food Inspector and another [2011 (1) SCC 176], the Apex Court held that the Laboratories where samples of articles of food or adulterants may be analysed by the public analyst is in accordance with Section 23(1A)(ee) and 23(1A)(hh) of the PFA Act.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings Pvt.Ltd. v. Food Inspector and another [2011 (1) SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Evidently,
the report of the public analyst in this case is not in conformity with Section 23(1A)(ee) and M.I.Sunny vs State Of Kerala on 27 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105498302/
2 23(1A)(hh) of the PFA Act.

entities.text: M.I.Sunny vs State Of Kerala on 27 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence the lodging of the complaint before the trial court was based on an erroneous report of the public analyst and the trial court went wrong in taking cognizance of the offences against the accused on the strength of Ext.P12.
Hence the conviction and sentence imposed against the revision petitioner/1st accused is manifestly illegal and is liable to be set aside.

8. The judgment of conviction and sentence rendered by the trial court, which has been confirmed in ..6..
appeal, is set aside.
The revision petitioner/1 st accused is found not guilty of the offences enumerated hereinabove and accordingly he is acquitted.
Cancelling his bail bond, this Court directs that he be set at liberty.
If any fine amount is deposited during the pendency of the proceedings, the same shall be released to the revision petitioner/1st accused in accordance with law.
Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.
The criminal revision petition is allowed accordingly.

Sd/-
N.ANIL KUMAR, JUDGE skj M.I.Sunny vs State Of Kerala on 27 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105498302/
